readme: SCOPE-7's token file. Generated from the contract and from nothing else; no value here was invented.

People read the contract, tests read this file: the plugins service, the registry (SCOPE-9) and a new client (SCOPE-10) each fail their tests on a value this file does not list for them, and on one it lists for them that they do not handle and that is neither `reserved` nor `retired` (SCOPE-8).

`emitter` and `acceptor` are arrays of party strings from `parties`; §0.8's Callers letters map onto them as C client, P panel, B bot, G guest. `registry` covers the bot and the signer where an entry is not the bot's alone.
A `service-only` entry is listed with no members and for no party: it is outside SCOPE-8's two-way test, and neither the registry's scan nor the client's expects or forbids one.

`pending` is what SCOPE-7 says this file carries and the contract does not yet record. Each record names what is missing, who owes it, the version that lands it and what the floor asserts until then. The generator refuses to run once the contract records one of them and no extractor has been written.

pending.what: the one fixed registry reason string each of `A_YANK` and `A_REMOVAL_REQUEST` carries
pending.why: BOT-80 says an `A_*` entry's `reason` is "the one fixed registry string SCOPE-7's file lists for that code", and §0.8 records no string. The service's decision type carries `public_reason`, which is NULL by design for an author action, so the first author yank either fails a body check or carries an invented string that the registry silently substitutes its own copy for.
pending.owed_by: astra-plugins-ops (contract version ops.15, §0.8); minice-be's half is §1.3 row 8.5
pending.floor: until ops.15 lands, `fixed_reasons` is null and the selftest asserts that it is null and that this record is present; from ops.15 it is two non-empty strings and the selftest asserts that.

pending.what: FLOW-13's reason-code table, one entry per code with its level, stage, `fix`, panel-only flag, title and remedy
pending.why: n8 publishes the table inside this file rather than in one of its own, so that the panel, SCOPE-1's comparison and the canary read one artifact at one commit. The codes themselves live in the bot's `bot/lib/codes.mjs` and `POLICY_CODES`, not in the contract, so this generator cannot read them: registry `bot/gen-codes-table.mjs` (B-T2.3) emits the table and this program merges it through --codes.
pending.lands_with: B-T2.3, with or after this file
pending.floor: without --codes the table is null and the selftest asserts that it is null and that this record is present; with --codes it asserts one entry per code, each carrying all six members.

pending.what: the generated-workflow template list: every version `init-ci` has emitted, with the author audience and author-notify path it compiles
pending.why: SCOPE-7 requires the list and the contract names no entry of it. ID-73 forbids marking an audience or the notify path `retired` while a listed template compiles it, so an empty list is not the same claim as a list with template `1` in it: the empty one lets a later regeneration retire a name that authors' repositories still compile.
pending.floor: until ops.15 lands, `templates` is an empty array, this record is present, and nothing may be marked `retired` on the strength of it; from ops.15 the selftest asserts at least one template, each with an audience, a notify path and a state.

pending.why: B-T3.11 compiles its `plugin_not_listed` expectation and its closing ordinary read from these two and from nothing else: every CLIENT-80 operation that can answer `plugin_not_listed` sits behind a bearer that job does not hold, and `GET cards/{plugin_id}` is not routed until a MINOR records OPEN-MBE-32 (attack M-8).
pending.owed_by: minice-be (§1.3 row 8.6, accepted as its W-6)
pending.lands_with: the version that publishes them; ops.22 at the latest, before R3
pending.floor: until that version lands, `service_only` carries the four categories SCOPE-8 names and this record says the two paths are absent; from then the selftest asserts both paths are present, with no members and no party, which is what B-T3.11 compiles against.

pending.what: the public report-outcome code vocabulary `reports.mine` may return
pending.why: CLIENT-80's `reports.mine` returns an `outcome`, "a public code or null", and no party has written the list down (attack m-2). The client branches on it to render a reporter's own reports, so a floor that counts the schema and not this list leaves the client's SCOPE-10 scan passing vacuously over a vocabulary a human reporter actually reads.
pending.owed_by: minice-be supplies the enumeration (accepted as its W-16); either plan publishes it into §0.8
pending.floor: until that version lands the client-side floor is written for B.3's four report states alone and this record says the outcome list is not floored; from then it counts both.
